items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing the New York
state teachers' retirement system to accept alternate methods of postal mail
for submittal of forms and applications
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6513

SPONSOR: MANNION
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to authorizing the New
York state teachers' retirement system to accept alternate methods of
postal mail for submittal of forms and applications

 
PURPOSE OF THE BILL:  This bill amends Education Law Section 508 to
authorize NYSTRS to accept alternate methods of postal mail services and
offer expanded options to the membership for submitting and filing
retirement system forms and applications.

 
SUMMARY AND JUSTIFICATION:

Pursuant to current law, certain forms and documents must be filed with
the System within a prescribed period of time or by a specified date in
order for a member to be eligible for a benefit. Although the membership
has various options for submitting forms and documents to the System,
including online and faxing options, members have the option to mail
forms to the Systan. In addition, there are certain forms that require a
postal mailing - the Election of Retirement Benefit form which selects
the option and/or beneficiary, Designation of Beneficiary for In-Service
or Post-Retirement Paragraph 2 Death Benefit and Election to Reinstate
are just some examples.

For the form/designation to be deemed filed on the day it was mailed, or
what is referred to "same day filing", the law requires such mailing
must be through the United States postal service registered or certified
mail or through an equivalent service through the United States postal
service. Based on the law as written, the System is bound to provide for
postal mail options which are offered only through the United States
Postal Service.

This specific provision was last amended in 2003 and there are other
methods of postal mail tracking services to be utilized providing a
similar option to certified or registered mail through the United States
Postal Service. The Retirement Board seeks authority to provide for
those alternate postal methods through rule and regulation.

The System recognizes many members use alternate postal methods for many
reasons, such as the business operating hours extend beyond the United
States Postal Service and some of these methods are more convenient and
accessible to our membership. For many, the business hours of the United
States Postal Service may be limiting and accessing equivalent postal
services offered by other providers will provide more locations and
provide extended hours of operation. The law as written, however, places
limitations on these alternate mailing avenues. Currently, if the
membership utilizes such alternate postal mailing options, the document
is not deemed filed with the system on the date mailed, but rather the
date the document is received by the system, leaving some members fail-
ing to meet the statutory deadlines and possibly impacting the filing
intentions.  As a clarification, regardless of the postal mailing
service selected, the statutory requirement that no such document shall
be deemed filed with the retirement system on the date of mailing unless
actually received by the retirement system will remain.


By authorizing NYSTRS to accept alternate forms of tracked postal mail,
this legislation will provide options for our members to meet deadlines
and file system documents timely. The Retirement System respectfully
seeks authority to provide for these alternate mail tracking services,
not only for customer service, but also to update the statute to reflect
other contemporary options.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE OF THE BILL:

This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law; provided, however, that effective immediately, the New
York state teachers' retirement system is hereby authorized to promul-
gate any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation of this act
on its effective date.

 
OTHER AGENCIES TO WHOM THE BILL MAY BE OF INTEREST:

Division of the Budget, Department of Financial Services.

 
BUDGETARY IMPLICATIONS OF THE BILL:

It is estimated there will be no annual cost to the employers of members
of the New York State Teachers' Retirement System if this bill is
enacted.
